title: Learn, Earn or Quit: Garry Tan's career framework for choosing jobs in 2022
summary: Garry Tan argues every job should be judged by whether you are learning, earning, or both, and that you should quit if it is neither. Early in a career, learn first by building real things or winning real customers, then earn, ideally through equity, while avoiding the hedonic treadmill.

principles.text: Judge any job by two tests: are you learning, are you earning? If neither, leave.
principles.quote: are you learning or are you earning if both you're in a great place if it's one or the other that's good too if it's neither it's time to move on you're wasting your life

principles.text: Early in your career, learn first, then earn. Reversing the order risks slow learning and the hedonic treadmill.
principles.quote: learn first then earn that's the best strategy if you try and do it in reverse and you try to earn first you'll probably still learn but maybe slowly

principles.text: Hustlers break in by doing the work unasked: build the improvement for a product you like, or send founders customers.
principles.quote: if you see a product website or service that you like and you have some improvements you can suggest you gotta build it or design it or write it yourself and then cold email them

principles.text: Don't wait for the perfect problem. Start building something real; you only learn creating by doing.
principles.quote: it just has to be a real problem that your software can actually solve

principles.text: A great thing you made beats a credential and puts you in the top 10 percent without a pedigree.
principles.quote: when you create something impressive that users love it's better than a credential

principles.text: Equity is the highest form of earning, and founders or early employees can learn while they earn.
principles.quote: to make the most amount of money you need to create true wealth by owning the stock of a company that became worth a lot of money
